text: Expose modular invariance in a Lagrangian lattice, unfold wrapping orbits, impose level matching by strip integration, and resum the Scherk–Schwarz momentum. The sequence distinguishes a physical light closed-string tower from non-level-matched terms in the original integrand.

Resum compact momenta, transform characters when changing worldsheet channel, and retain all topology-dependent factors. The resulting massless transverse coefficients permit tadpole factorization. Resummation alone can also reorganize a direct-channel amplitude without changing its physical channel.

One-loop vacuum amplitudes combine torus, Klein bottle, annulus and Möbius strip contributions. Poisson resummation, unfolding the modular fundamental domain, and modified-Bessel-function asymptotics isolate dominant KK contributions from exponentially suppressed heavy states.

Expand oscillator characters, resum m9 alone, and integrate proper time. Retain transverse momenta and Wilson-line shifts in the effective tower mass. Comparing that mass to lambda identifies which sectors can survive the low-breaking-scale limit.

T-dual brane geometry supplies spectrum counting and candidate extrema. A complementary Schwinger proper-time supertrace, expanded in Cartan Wilson lines, relates quadratic masses to differences between bosonic and fermionic Dynkin indices.

Replace explicit stack-by-stack momentum shifts with matrix traces, then transform each topology to its transverse channel. This representation separates brane-distribution information from universal character and lattice factors and exposes the tadpole condition.

Use I = βG, G = M−TS−ΩHJ and the first law to differentiate thermodynamic quantities. A change-of-variables argument relates the fixed-(M,J) entropy correction to minus the higher-derivative Euclidean action evaluated on Kerr.

Regulate the Euclidean Einstein action at a large-radius boundary and subtract a matching flat-space action. Boundary falloffs show that its first variation vanishes at fixed T and ΩH; higher-derivative boundary terms decay at infinity.

Evaluate curvature-invariant integrals with computer algebra using x = cosθ, integrating x before the radial coordinate. Express results through τ = 2πT/ΩH, then perturbatively invert the grand-canonical relations to obtain fixed-(M,J) corrections.

Evaluate leading large-distance forces from gauge charges, masses or tensions, and moduli derivatives. The brane force coefficient contains gauge repulsion minus the scalar inner product minus gravitational attraction; tension derivatives hold the Planck scale fixed.

Track radion-dependent masses, tensions and kinetic terms through circle reduction, then include axions and graviphoton charge. Appendix A uses a nonrelativistic radial Schrödinger problem to distinguish classical attraction from quantum binding.

Linearize the ExFT field equations, evaluate internal derivatives through the embedding tensor and harmonic generators, and diagonalize finite matrices level by level. Tensor equations require Stückelberg gauge fixing and yield first-order equations for topologically massive two-forms.

For another stationary point of the same lower-dimensional theory, dress the original twist, embedding tensor and harmonic generators with a constant E6(6) matrix representing that vacuum. The authors apply the resulting mass operators without rebuilding harmonics of the deformed metric.

Start from a generalized Scherk–Schwarz reduction with twist U and weight ρ, then multiply the generalized-frame expressions by an infinite tower of scalar harmonics. The twist carries tensor structure, allowing scalar harmonics to describe fluctuations of every bosonic spin.

Linearize ExFT equations and replace internal differentiation by dressed harmonic-action matrices T_A. Mass matrices depend on X and T; scalar contributions organize as XX+XT+TT. Diagonalized modes can be mapped back through the ExFT/supergravity dictionary.

Use generalized Scherk-Schwarz reduction and a global generalized frame satisfying L_UM UN=X_MN^P UP. Dressing the frame with the vacuum scalar vielbein produces the corresponding dressed embedding tensor.

Expand every fluctuation using the same complete basis of scalar harmonics; the generalized vielbein carries its tensor structure. Choose harmonics at the maximally symmetric scalar configuration, which need not itself solve the equations of motion.
Can a simple gravitational model describe a strongly coupled 2+1-dimensional system with a charged condensate, a superconducting transition and a gap in its frequency-dependent conductivity?

In weakly coupled unitary extensions of Einstein gravity, does semiclassical black-hole entropy exceed the number of light species, and is Einstein entropy minimal at fixed mass? The paper also investigates analogous AdS black-brane entropy-density statements.

Can natural scalar masses coexist with the weak gravity conjecture at very small gauge charge? The authors also seek a generalization to product Abelian groups and models in which a hypothetical fifth-force discovery could test electroweak naturalness.
Is the WGC preserved under toroidal compactification and scalar stabilization, what strengthening accommodates KK photons, and how far can black-hole extremality arguments extend to axions?

Can Maldacena–Nuñez-type restrictions on Minkowski and de Sitter flux vacua also obstruct AdS vacua whose KK masses are parametrically above the cosmological curvature scale? What would this imply for classical Romans-mass smoothing of O6 singularities?

How do torus geometry and brane distributions control the spectrum and vacuum energy in D-dimensional orientifolds with a single Scherk–Schwarz direction? Corner backgrounds reduce the brane data to integer multiplicities paired across that direction.
Can Scherk–Schwarz compactifications of open string theory have exponentially suppressed or positive one-loop vacuum energy without developing tachyonic Wilson-line moduli?

How do orientifold-compatible brane positions determine the massless spectrum and one-loop vacuum energy after supersymmetry is broken along a circle? The T-dual description makes Wilson lines geometric and separates endpoint half-branes from mirror-paired stacks.

How do six- and eight-derivative gravitational EFT operators change Kerr thermodynamics at first order, can those changes be obtained without the corrected metric, and when do entropy corrections have definite signs?
How should the superextremality-based WGC and long-range Repulsive Force Conjecture be distinguished with multiple photons and massless scalars, and could a stronger principle imply both?

Can exceptional field theory efficiently determine KK masses and identify the corresponding higher-dimensional fluctuations, including lower-spin sectors mixed by background fluxes, when residual isometries provide little help?

How can exceptional field theory compute Kaluza-Klein masses and identify higher-dimensional mass eigenstates around vacua in maximal consistent truncations, including backgrounds with few or no surviving symmetries?

What rigorous restrictions do higher-dimensional equations place on Kaluza–Klein masses and scale separation, and can Romans mass replace the problematic O6 loci in promising supersymmetric AdS4 compactifications by smooth local geometry?

Can axion models of early dark energy be embedded in quantum gravity, and how strongly does the axion weak gravity conjecture constrain their decay constants and cosmologically relevant energy fractions?
Can gravitational production from a hot Standard Model brane supply viable dark matter in the dark dimension, while relating its abundance to the dark-energy scale?

Can a micron-scale dark dimension accommodate neutrino masses, produce distinguishable cosmological and local signals from dynamical KK-graviton dark matter, and support inflation despite the light spin-2 tower?

How do flux compactifications stabilize moduli and determine the sign and size of vacuum energy? Can they yield parametrically controlled metastable de Sitter or AdS vacua with decoupled massive towers?

What linear cosmological signatures arise from repeated decays within a dark-matter KK-graviton tower, and what do CMB, BAO and weak-lensing data imply for its kick velocity and Dark Dimension parameters?
Can the asymptotic WGC extend to gravity-coupled 3D EFTs from finite-volume M-theory compactifications on K3×K3, including a proposed strong-coupling counterpart?
Can classical type IIA flux compactifications stabilize all geometric moduli, and admit explicit families with parametrically large volume, weak coupling and a valid four-dimensional description?

Which geometric restrictions distinguish continuous moduli spaces of consistent quantum gravity from those of nongravitational field theories, and what constraints follow for effective theories, inflation and axions?

Boundary conditions are investigated through nonlinear Frobenius-type power series and backward numerical evolution. Matching uses initial data from the perturbative weak-coupling solution; robustness tests include approximately 10^5 random evolutions and another approximately 10^5 with up to 10% boundary-data noise.

Combining internal and external Einstein equations removes the indefinite warp Laplacian and bounds a Bakry–Émery Ricci tensor. Existing weighted-Laplacian eigenvalue theorems then constrain the universally decoupled spin-two tower, rather than estimating its masses from integrated scalar-curvature ratios.

Pure-form supersymmetry equations, Bianchi identities and orientifold parities are reduced using the imposed local symmetry. Algebraic constraints and radial-coordinate freedom leave seven first-order equations; the chosen radial gauge sets g_rr=e^(−2A).

The cosmological translation adds the axion to a specified ΛCDM background with Ω0,M=0.31, Ω0,R=9×10⁻⁵ and ΩΛ=0.69. Starting at rest with χ0=(π−0.01)f, the author fits the axion density evolution to a phenomenological EDE interpolation to obtain ac and fEDE.

The instanton action is related to the potential amplitude through mχ²=ΛUV⁴e^(−S)/feff². Substitution into the axion WGC produces an n-independent inequality involving feff and a logarithm of ΛUV⁴/(feff²mχ²). The bound is evaluated for representative EDE parameters.

Compute zero-spatial-momentum conductivity from an Ax perturbation with e^{-iωt} dependence and ingoing horizon boundary conditions. Use its boundary coefficients for linear response and Kramers–Kronig relations to associate an imaginary pole with a real conductivity delta function.

Numerically integrate the coupled nonlinear radial scalar and electrostatic equations from regular horizon data to the boundary, impose one vanishing scalar coefficient, and fit the resulting condensate curves near the critical temperature.

A tortoise-coordinate Klein–Gordon analysis motivates effectively massless radial propagation near a simple horizon. The authors then use a flat-space 1PI graviton propagator and Källén–Lehmann spectral positivity to argue for enhanced gravitational couplings.

Integrate the first law dS=β(M)dM and use β≥RS together with the asserted radius relation RS;X=M[1+IX(M)] in Planck units. Combine the resulting entropy estimate with an imported semiclassical evaporation bound.

Wald entropy is expressed using an effective coupling for r,t-polarized gravitons. For Lovelock branes, the analysis examines purely spatial Riemann components at the horizon and argues that their higher-curvature entropy contributions vanish.

Direct dimensional reduction of massive IIA supergravity gives a zero-mode potential including flux and O6 contributions. Eliminating the nondynamical spacetime-polarized F4 fixes the RR axion combination; extrema and quadratic fluctuation masses are then analyzed.

Using the imported orientifold effective-action framework, the authors solve D_iW=0 with W=∫Ω_c∧H3+e0+e_a t^a+(1/2)κ_abc m^a t^b t^c−(m0/6)κ_abc t^a t^b t^c. Complex-structure and Kähler equations decouple; the dilaton is fixed afterward.
Compare explicit moduli-space metrics, geodesic distances and light spectra in compactification limits, including changes to Einstein frame and quotients by discrete dualities.

Estimate one-loop corrections to scalar kinetic terms after integrating out a generically heavy particle with moduli-dependent mass. The authors find that finitely many particles becoming massless do not themselves generate infinite distance for D > 2; an infinite tower can do so.

For Calabi–Yau vector moduli, analyze the integrated scalar curvature through the first Chern class and Kähler form, decomposing it into compactification and singularity contributions. Infinite-distance singularities are asserted to contribute negatively.

Generalizes black-hole decay kinematics using charge and energy conservation. Mass-fraction weights give Z=Σσ_i z_i with Σσ_i<1; convex geometry of particle and antiparticle charge-to-mass vectors translates this into a discharge criterion.

Uses cutoff-sensitive scalar mass corrections δm²=Λ²(aq²+bλ)/(16π²), then compares the natural physical scalar mass with the WGC charge-to-mass requirement. The coefficients a,b encode ultraviolet sensitivity.

Generate charged black branes from the Horowitz–Strominger solutions by lifting and dimensional reduction; rotate scalar combinations into coupled and decoupled fields. Lift charged black holes to strings, boost along the compact direction, and reduce to obtain mixed KK charges and ADM extremality bounds.

Evaluate Euclidean instanton actions with Gibbons–Hawking–York boundary terms, reduce the on-shell action to boundary contributions, and minimize over the core parameter. Compare the resulting boundary expression with the higher-dimensional ADM mass.

Replace a direct calculation of the lowest nonzero internal Laplacian eigenvalue by the estimate MKK^(2−d) ∼ ∫√gd e^(4A)Rd. Dimensional analysis and a quoted Lichnerowicz result motivate this proxy; the actual KK spectrum is not computed.

Repeat the integrated argument with an e^(2φ) weight. This weight is selected using a classical scaling symmetry; integrating the weighted dilaton equation by parts introduces a dilaton-gradient term into the denominator of the curvature-ratio diagnostic.

Use traced external and internal Einstein equations to express curvature integrals through flux energies, dilaton gradients, and source tensions. In ten dimensions, the integrated dilaton equation eliminates the NS-flux contribution and exposes positivity bounds.

Numerically solves coupled Boltzmann equations for individual KK abundances, including brane production, decays back to Standard Model fields, and intratower daughter production. Early production also receives an analytic treatment using Bessel-function kernels.

Dimensional analysis of universal graviton–stress-tensor coupling estimates brane-to-bulk production. The expansion-compensated quantity y=ρKK/s gives production dominated by the initial temperature, conditional on approximate preservation of dark-sector mass.

The neutrino analysis uses an infinite KK decomposition and Dirac mass matrix, with volume-suppressed brane–bulk masses m_i^D ≈ y_i⟨H⟩/√(R MUV). Oscillation probabilities are parametrized by the six standard oscillation parameters plus R and the lightest Dirac-mass parameter.

Following the earlier DDG model, a lifetime-threshold estimate assumes states heavier than the mass corresponding to lifetime t have already decayed. This yields characteristic mass evolution m_l ∝ t^(-2/7); the visible decay width scales cubically with mass. High-redshift normalization is then propagated to the local universe.

Dimensional reduction and Weyl rescaling to Einstein frame; extremization of the universal volume/dilaton potential; comparison with traced, integrated higher-dimensional Einstein and dilaton equations.

Integrated Bianchi identities impose tadpoles. Internal Laplacian eigenvalues estimate KK masses; holographic scalar dimensions diagnose scale separation once operators dual to KK modes are identified.

Restrict weak lensing to estimated linear scales using k_NL^3 P_lin(k_NL,z)/(2π^2)=Δ_NL. Apply redshift-dependent multipole cuts, requiring cross-bin measurements to pass both cuts; compare Δ_NL=0.5 and 1.0.

Modify CLASS and sample v_today alongside six ΛCDM parameters with MontePython. Use Planck 2018 temperature, polarization and lensing, BAO, and KiDS-1000 band powers; sampling uses Metropolis–Hastings, with nested sampling for KiDS-only analyses.

Model the background momentum distribution with a moving Gaussian-like peak and fixed width parameter η=0.25. Use distribution moments and a fluid approximation truncating the Boltzmann hierarchy at multipole ℓ_max=2; shear terms are retained in the full analysis.

Test the repulsive-force inequality by comparing Coulomb repulsion with scalar-gradient attraction, using mass homogeneity and inverse kinetic matrices. The classical gravitational-force coefficient vanishes at D=3.
Expand the Kähler form along a scaling parameter λ, organize quartic intersections, reduce the bosonic supergravity action, and extract charge-dependent couplings using gq²=g3D² qa G^ab qb.
